nodes.description: Because GPVI signalling is the route by which collagen recruits the amplification machinery, its loss removes both the aggregation and the secretion response to collagen specifically. Dense granule ATP secretion is normal to ADP but absent to collagen in the Belgian proband; collagen-, convulxin- and collagen-related-peptide-induced aggregation and serotonin release were absent in all four Chilean families. The platelets are structurally normal and the granules themselves are intact - this is a failure to trigger secretion, not a storage pool defect, which is the distinction from gray platelet syndrome and the Hermansky-Pudlak group.
nodes.id: Absent Collagen-Induced Aggregation and Granule Secretion

nodes.description: The direct molecular consequence: the collagen-binding receptor is missing from the platelet membrane. In the Chilean homozygotes flow cytometry and Western blotting confirm loss of the full-length protein, with the truncated product detectable only in permeabilized platelets, and the Fc receptor gamma-chain that partners GPVI in the membrane is partially reduced while other platelet receptors and signalling proteins are unaffected. This specificity is what makes the disorder a clean receptor-loss phenotype rather than a general platelet defect. Where the allele is missense rather than truncating, the residual protein is present but cannot bind collagen - the R38C substitution abolished collagen binding when introduced into recombinant GPVI-Fc.

nodes.description: There is no disease-specific therapy and none is needed for most affected individuals. Management follows the general approach to an inherited platelet function disorder with mild bleeding risk: an antifibrinolytic or desmopressin first, with platelet transfusion reserved for when those are insufficient or for surgical cover. No trial has been conducted in GP6 deficiency specifically, so this is the inherited-platelet-disorder recommendation applied to a disorder at the mild end of that group.

nodes.description: GP6 encodes platelet glycoprotein VI. Three classes of disease allele are documented: a homozygous single-adenine insertion in exon 6 (c.711_712insA) that introduces a premature stop at residue 242, before the transmembrane domain, so the truncated protein cannot reach the membrane; out-of-frame deletions and insertions that abolish the transcript or the protein; and missense substitutions in the ligand-binding immunoglobulin-like domains (R38C, S175N) that leave a protein unable to bind collagen or to be expressed normally at the surface. Because the mechanism is loss of function on both alleles, the quantitative and qualitative alleles converge on the same mechanism.

nodes.description: GPVI is the activating, not the adhesive, collagen receptor: platelets lacking it still tether to collagen but do not switch on. Patient platelets show no aggregation and no secretion to collagen, convulxin or the collagen-related peptide, while responses to ADP and other agonists are preserved - the pharmacological signature of a single receptor loss. Spreading on collagen, and on von Willebrand factor, is abolished. The defect is agonist-specific, which is why a routine platelet count and most of a standard aggregometry panel are normal.

nodes.description: Targeted disruption of GP VI in the mouse reproduces the human laboratory phenotype closely: null platelets do not aggregate to fibrillar collagen or convulxin, and thrombus formation on collagen under flow is abolished while initial tethering to the surface is normal. Tail bleeding time is not severely prolonged - which parallels the mild human diathesis and is the observation that launched GPVI as an antithrombotic target.

nodes.description: The clinical output: lifelong mucocutaneous bleeding that is mild relative to Glanzmann thrombasthenia or the severe signalling defects, with a normal platelet count and normal platelet morphology. Severity is the point of the entry rather than a footnote: GPVI loss blocks the thrombotic contribution of collagen without disabling haemostasis, which is exactly the property that makes the receptor an antithrombotic drug target.

nodes.description: The step that explains why the bleeding is mild. In flow-chamber studies of whole blood from the Chilean homozygotes, aggregate formation and phosphatidylserine exposure on collagen and on a non-collagen surface were blocked, and thrombin generation was partially reduced - but adhesion itself was retained. So the patient keeps the first arm of primary haemostasis (platelets still stick) and loses the amplification and procoagulant arms. The thrombin-generation deficit has been shown independently in GPVI-deficient platelet-rich plasma, and is mechanistically interesting because GPVI also binds polymerized fibrin, so the receptor contributes to the coagulation side of thrombus growth and not only to the collagen response. The authors of the flow study read the retained adhesion as the likely reason the diathesis is mild, and as the explanation for why so few of the estimated homozygous individuals in Chile have been identified.
